headline: Metropolitan Expansion Investigation Includes New Charges Against Former President García
content: The investigation surrounding former president Alan Garcia has expanded following revelations about illicit payments linked to his administrations dealings with Brazilian construction giant Odebrecht. Authorities have now included charges of aggravated collusion and money laundering against him. The prosecutor José Domingo Pérez took decisive actions during a recent session which involved halting Garcia’s interrogation regarding the Lima metro project, adding these serious allegations to the preliminary investigations, and requesting travel restrictions for Garcia pending further judicial review.The developments come after reports surfaced indicating financial transactions through offshore accounts involving key figures within Garcias government.

headline: Former Presidential Advisor Faces Prison Sentence Over Allegations Linked To Corruption Scandal
content: In connection with ongoing corruption inquiries related to the infamous ‘Case of Cocktails’, advisors to detained political leader Keiko Fujimori were sentenced to three years of preventive detention. This decision was made by Judge Ricardo Concepción Carhuáncho based upon requests filed by Prosecutor José Domingo Pérez.Garcías associates, including Ana Herz de Vega and Pier Figari, along with attorney Vicente Silva Checa—who allegedly acted as an informal advisor—are implicated in receiving funds intended to support their partys campaign efforts.These individuals form part of what authorities describe as the core group responsible for managing illegal contributions funneled through intermediaries like congressperson Rolando Ruíz Egüez who facilitated connections between donors and recipients under strict directives issued directly from higher-ups within the organization.

headline: New Developments In Criminal Network Probe Link Fishing Magnate With Judiciary Malfeasance
content: Scar Peña Aparicio, known colloquially as the King of Illegal Fishing, finds himself entangled deeper within investigative proceedings targeting organized crime networks dubbed White Collars of the Port. According to sources close to the case led by Specialized Prosecution Office Coordinator Jorge Chavez Cotrina, there exists substantial evidence suggesting Peña engaged in corrupt practices aimed at influencing judiciary outcomes.Preliminary findings indicate he may have paid off judges such as Walter Rojas—a notable figure previously heading the Court of Appeals in Callao—to secure favorable rulings across various jurisdictions where his fishing operations required lenient oversight.This revelation adds another layer to existing probes examining systemic corruption affecting maritime law enforcement agencies throughout Peru.
